document.title: SRS: ACME Battery Recycling Control System (BRCS)
document.text:
# 1 Introduction
## 1.1 Purpose
This SRS specifies the requirements of the Battery Recycling Control System of the company ACME (BRCS) for its development. It is intended for the software engineers who will design and implement the system.
## 1.2 Scope
ACME currently recycles batteries in a fully manual way, which causes inefficient control of the process. The Battery Recycling Control System (BRCS) will automate the process and will be used by the operators and the managers of ACME. The BRCS will automatically control the separator, the shredder, the press, the distiller (which uses a metallic catalyst only with the powder of button batteries with manganese) and the conveyor belts, and will display the status of the process. The BRCS will not control the incinerator, the transport of the waste, or the sale of the recovered metals.
## 1.3 Product Overview
### 1.3.1 Product perspective
The system has the following interfaces.
- Separator, shredder, press, and distiller, see [REF-01]. - Conveyor belts (PLC), see [REF-03]. - Weight sensors of the output trays, see [REF-04]. - Three-layer architecture with an application server and a relational database on a dedicated server.
### 1.3.3 User characteristics
The users are the operators, who control the process, and the managers, who also access the configuration and the audit functions. The operators receive specific training on the system.
### 1.3.4 Limitations
The machines are controlled with the same communication scheme that is currently used. Only the managers access the configuration and audit functions. The system must be available during all the working hours of the plant, except in the case of a power outage.
## 1.4 Definitions
**Batch:** set of batteries (normal and button) with a maximum weight of 2000 kg. **Button battery with manganese:** small battery whose recycling requires distilling the powder with a metallic catalyst. **Separator:** machine that separates the batteries into three groups (button batteries with manganese, button batteries without manganese, and normal batteries). **Shredder:** machine that shreds normal batteries to obtain battery powder and waste. **Minimum weight of the shredder:** amount of normal batteries in the bucket required to start the shredder, which is 300 kg. **Press:** machine that presses button batteries to obtain battery powder and waste. **Distiller:** machine that recovers metals from the battery powder. **Operator:** person who uses the system to control the process.
## 1.5 SRS Overview
This SRS follows the outline of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018. The sections of the outline that do not appear have been omitted for simplicity; notice that this reason is valid only in the framework of this academic course. Requirements are identified as FUN(xx) for functional, PER(xx) for performance, and QUA(xx) for quality requirements. Each requirement is a singular sentence that uses the verb "shall".
# 2 References
[REF-01] Technical Manual of the Interfaces of the Recycling Machines (Annex B), ACME Engineering, version 1.4, 2009. [REF-02] The current environmental regulations. [REF-03] ACME Conveyor Belt Control Interface Specification, version 1.2, ACME Engineering, 2009.
# 3 Specific requirements
## 3.1 Functions
FUN(01) The system shall start the recycling process when the operator indicates that the separator is loaded with a batch. FUN(02) The system shall control the start and stop of the conveyor belts between the machines. FUN(03) The system should stop the separator when an output tray reaches the weight limit, which is 300 kg per battery type. FUN(04) The system shall allow configuring the weight limit of the output trays of the separator. FUN(05) The system shall start the shredder when a bucket of normal batteries reaches the minimum weight of the shredder. FUN(06) The system shall stop the shredder when the powder bucket reaches the maximum weight of the shredder. FUN(07) The system shall distill separately the battery powder from normal batteries and the powder from button batteries. FUN(08) The system shall add catalyst to all the battery powder before distilling it. FUN(09) The system shall start the separator and record the weight of the loaded batch. FUN(10) The system shall stop the distiller when the level of the output boxes is high. FUN(11) The system shall control the operation of the incinerator. FUN(12) The system shall run on a Siemens S7-1200 controller programmed in ladder logic. FUN(13) The system shall allow the managers to consult the audit log of the operations performed.
## 3.2 Performance requirements
PER(01) The system shall update the displayed status of the process at least every 2 seconds. PER(02) The system shall be available 99.999% of the working hours.
## 3.7 Software system attributes
QUA(01) The system shall display the status of the process in an intuitive and easy-to-understand way.
# 5 Appendixes
## 5.1 Assumptions and dependencies
The machines are assumed to work according to their technical manual.
## 5.2 Acronyms and abbreviations
**BRCS:** Battery Recycling Control System. **SRS:** Software Requirements Specification.
